Aakash Digital · EdTech · Live Doubt Resolution

Instant Doubt Solver

A zero-latency doubt-resolution platform that rebuilt the "raise your hand" moment for 3 lakh students learning online — live video, structured chat and snap-to-ask, engineered for India's real bandwidth, devices and exam-season anxiety.

01Context & Brief

When classrooms went online,
the doubt got left behind.

The pandemic moved India's largest coaching institute fully online overnight. Lectures survived the jump. The single most valuable moment — a confused student raising their hand — did not.

“

In a real classroom, a confused student could tap the teacher's shoulder after class. Online, that tap became a WhatsApp message that no one ever answered.

— Product Strategy Brief · Aakash Digital · 2021

What I owned

UX Strategy & Direction End-to-end Product Design Research & Synthesis Cross-platform Patterns Cross-functional Facilitation
02Problem

Three problems that kept
students stuck.

Each compounded the next — and together they put renewal revenue at risk. This is the chain we set out to break.

PROBLEM 01

The disappearing doubt

No reliable channel to ask during or after online class. Questions dropped into WhatsApp groups and were buried within minutes — confusion stacking as new topics built on unresolved ones.

73%doubts unanswered in 24h
PROBLEM 02

The human-bandwidth wall

One faculty member could not personally answer hundreds of daily doubts. With no triage, dedupe or auto-resolve, teachers burned 3+ hours a day re-answering the same questions.

1 : 350teacher to student ratio
PROBLEM 03

The trust cliff

Unable to get help, students drifted to YouTube and unofficial Telegram groups. Parents noticed. The premium promise — "your teacher is here for you" — began to crack at renewal time.

18%drop in renewal intent

What the analysis told us

INSIGHT 01

Friction, not fear, blocked questions

Students weren't shy — they were stuck describing a diagram or equation in text. When we let them photograph a question, willingness to ask jumped. The interface was the barrier, not motivation.

82% of doubts involved a figure or equation
INSIGHT 02

Repetition was eating faculty alive

Coding 1,900 threads showed more than a third were near-duplicates. Surfacing an existing answer before submission would reclaim hours of faculty time and shrink the queue at the source.

38% of threads were duplicates
INSIGHT 03

Trust was leaking to outside channels

When the official path was slow, students defaulted to YouTube and Telegram. Every doubt resolved off-platform was a crack in the premium promise — and a measurable renewal risk.

41% used unofficial sources weekly
INSIGHT 04

The network broke the moment, not the model

Live help failed most often at the edges — denied camera permissions, weak 3G, dropped sessions. Designing for graceful degradation wasn't polish; it was the difference between help and abandonment.

#1 cause of failed live sessions: permissions

Two users. Opposite realities.

A student on a mid-range Android over patchy 4G, and a faculty member answering from a desktop with a whiteboard. One system had to serve both.

How might we…

HMW 1

…make submitting a doubt — including a photo of a notebook — as effortless as sending a WhatsApp message?

HMW 2

…give faculty a tool that routes, dedupes and prioritises doubts so they reach 10× more students in the same hour?

HMW 3

…design a live video doubt session that feels like a 1:1 office hour yet scales to thousands at once?

HMW 4

…hold the edge cases — weak network, denied camera, teacher dropout — without breaking momentum or trust?

04Process

From evidence
to shipped.

01 · DISCOVER

Immersive research

412 surveys, 28 interviews, thread audit, drop-off analysis, WhatsApp-group observation.

02 · DEFINE

Baseline & blueprint

Quantified the before-state. Service blueprint across both users; trust-breaks pinpointed.

03 · DESIGN

Rapid prototyping

Lo-fi → hi-fi for 9 mobile and 5 web flows. Three iteration rounds with live panels.

04 · TEST

Usability validation

40 students across cities, on low-end devices. Surfaced critical permission & network cases.

05 · SHIP

Phased rollout

Async upload → text chat → live video → in-class overlay. Rolled out to 3L+ students.

05Solution

Three modes.
One seamless flow.

Doubt resolution isn't one action — it's a spectrum. We built three complementary modes students and faculty move between fluidly, by urgency, complexity and bandwidth.

Mode 01 · Snap, crop & submit

The 10-second doubt

82% of doubts involved a figure or equation — impossible to type. So photo became the primary input: point at the notebook, crop to the exact question, add optional context, submit. Under ten seconds, and it lands instantly in the faculty queue.

In-app cropper removes any need to edit photos first
Subject & chapter auto-tagged from session context
Confirmation animation = instant psychological closure
Text-only fallback when camera is denied
Submit
Crop
Mode 02 · Live 1:1 video

The whiteboard moment

Calculus derivations and reaction mechanisms can't be solved in text — they need a teacher's pen, live. A bespoke session experience for teaching: whiteboard as the primary surface, the student's question pinned on screen, a shared timer, and media controls both sides trust.

Whiteboard-first — teacher draws while the doubt stays visible
Session timer creates shared, respectful urgency
Tap-to-reveal controls keep explanations distraction-free
Graceful camera-off state survives bandwidth drops
Live session
Pinned doubt
Mode 03 · Structured chat

Async clarity at scale

Mid-complexity doubts don't need a call. A structured chat thread gives students timestamped answers with formatted equations, images and step-by-step breakdowns — and lets faculty resolve 8–12 in the time a single video takes. A post-resolution rating powers a quality flywheel.

Threads persist — referenceable during exam revision
Per-resolution rating surfaces star faculty
Pinned state keeps unresolved doubts from slipping
Chat thread
Feedback

Built for India's
real devices.

9 use cases, 100+ screens, designed at 360×740 — the sweet spot for India's dominant mid-range Android. Every interaction tested on 3G and against thumb-reach zones.

9
Escalation & alerts — edge cases

Network drops, mutes, timeouts, camera failures — every edge case mapped and designed. The rule: never strand the student. Each error recovers automatically, gives a clear next action, or routes to an alternative. Time warnings fire at 2 minutes and 30 seconds.

07Web Experience

Faculty-grade tools for

5 flows, 60+ screens, designed at 1440px with a multi-panel layout — queue, active session and whiteboard at once. Students on web get a mirrored, full-browser experience.

09Learnings

Six lessons that
travel forward.

📸

The input is the interface

Students didn't want a form — they wanted to point a camera. The biggest win wasn't a clever pattern, it was deleting the gap between "I have a doubt" and "doubt submitted": 90 seconds down to under 10.

💭

Anxiety, not just usability

Standard testing revealed task flows. Watching emotion revealed the product — relief at a confirmation, dread at a vanished doubt. Designing for anxiety is a different craft than designing for efficiency.

🔗

Two users, one system

Every faculty tool that made answering easier directly sped up student resolution. The queue-management work no student ever sees mattered as much as any student-facing screen.

📶

Design for the real network

Everything was tested at 3G with simulated packet loss. The video → audio → text → async fallback meant no student was ever fully stuck — and that's what carried us in Tier 2 & 3 cities.

🔔

Permission timing is a trust decision

Asking for the camera on first open: 31% grant. Asking at the moment a student requested video — when the why was obvious: 84%. We rebuilt the entire permission flow on this single finding.

🔄

Feedback loops compound

The one-tap rating wasn't metrics hygiene. It surfaced exceptional faculty, revealed content gaps producing repeat doubts, and gave students closure. Tiny loops × 3 lakh students became our product radar.
